title: 3D mapping of the Wolf-Rayet nebula M 1-67: clues for post-common envelope evolution in massive stars

evidence.locator: Sect. 1: an estimated distance of 6.4 (+2.5, −0.8) kpc, from Jiménez-Hernández et al. (2020). Sect. 2: 17 spectra at 15 slit positions with the Manchester Echelle Spectrometer on the 2.1 m telescope at San Pedro Mártir, a velocity resolution of 12 km/s. Sect. 4: three concentric structures, each a torus and a bipolar structure; "each bipolar lobe is modelled by a hollow ellipsoidal component squished at the waist"; "the three bipolar structures are contained within the plane of the sky and their symmetry axis are tilted with a PA = −40°"; velocities increase linearly with distance, v(r) = A (r/B). Table 2, inner, middle and outer structure: hollow ellipsoid a_out 35.0, 55.0, 55.0 arcsec; a_inn 25.0, 43.0, 46.0; b_out 15.8, 24.2, 35.8; b_inn 11.3, 18.9, 29.9; squish 0.55, 0.56, 0.35; v(r) = 90 (r/35), 90 (r/55), 90 (r/55) km/s; torus r_out 30.0, 50.0, 60.0 arcsec; r_inn 13.8, 25.0, 30.0; thickness 14.0, 25.0, 30.0; v(r) = 60 (r/30), 60 (r/50), 60 (r/60) km/s. Sect. 4: the model "does not model physical density"; two jets at apparent position angles 120° and 129°, expanding away at 15° and 55° from the plane of the sky, 75 and 56 arcsec long; blowouts on the receding side. Sect. 5: "it is very likely that there is only a single toroidal structure". Sect. 6: a kinematic age of 11.8 (+4.6, −0.8) kyr; the torus expands at 30 to 60 km/s, the bipolar structure at up to 90 km/s. Data availability: shared on reasonable request.
